project: RLQAS Phase 2 Fix001: Correct Partial-Circuit Architecture Search
description: Fix a critical bug in UCCSearchEnv where the RL agent's excitation-operator selection has no effect on the reported energy. All agents currently receive near-FCI energy after their first action regardless of which operator they choose, because (a) the classical optimizer inside step() is free to vary ALL UCCSD parameters, not just those corresponding to the selected operators, and (b) the circuit returned by build_circuit() always carries the full UCCSD object so the simulator bypasses the partial circuit. Fix these two bugs, re-validate that genuine architecture-search benchmarks (where the agent must discover good operators to achieve chemical accuracy) still pass, and generate honest benchmark results comparing PPO/DQN/A2C/SAC-Discrete on LiH.

phaseDependencies.phase1: RLQAS_Phase1_006 (Integrated package) — Phase 1 environment code is the primary target of the fix
phaseDependencies.phase2_full: RLQAS_Phase2_full — all six Phase 2 tasks are complete; this fix corrects the evaluation logic without restructuring them

background.summary: Two interlocking bugs make UCCSearchEnv report full-UCCSD energy regardless of agent actions.

bug_A.description: When run_classical_opt=True, the code minimizes energy_func(p) = circuit_builder.evaluate_energy(build_circuit(selected_ops, p), p). Both build_circuit and evaluate_energy internally call self.ucc.energy(params), which evaluates the FULL UCCSD ansatz over ALL n_params parameters. The optimizer (L-BFGS-B) is free to vary every element of p — including those for operators the RL agent has NOT selected. Starting from all-zeros, it converges to the full-UCCSD minimum, achieving near-FCI accuracy regardless of the agent's choice.
bug_A.correct_behavior: The optimizer must only vary parameters for the excitation operators currently in self.current_excitations. All other parameters must be held at zero. This way the objective being minimized is the VQE energy of the partial circuit (only the selected operators), not the full UCCSD.

bug_B.lines: shortcut block at top of compute_energy (~line 70-78)
bug_B.description: build_circuit() attaches circuit.ucc = self.ucc and circuit.params = params to every circuit object. compute_energy() detects these attributes and returns circuit.ucc.energy(circuit.params) — the full UCCSD energy with whatever params are stored on the circuit object. Because bug A has already placed full-UCCSD-optimal params on the circuit, this shortcut compounds the error. Even if bug A is fixed, this shortcut could silently reintroduce full-UCCSD evaluation if circuit.params is not masked properly.
bug_B.correct_behavior: compute_energy() must NOT use the circuit.ucc shortcut. It should evaluate the energy of the actual circuit that was constructed, which represents only the selected operators with their optimized (partial) parameters.

background.consequence: Every RL agent (PPO, DQN, A2C, SAC-Discrete) reports operator_count=1 and energy_error≈4e-9 Ha — well below FCI — after picking any single operator. The benchmark in results/algorithm_comparison/ppo_dqn_a2c_sacd_lih_10q.json is therefore meaningless: the agents are not doing architecture search.

objectives.description: Fix the classical optimizer in UCCSearchEnv.step() to optimize only the active parameters

Define energy_func_partial(theta) where theta has length len(active_param_indices); construct full-length params p = self.current_params.copy() then set p[active_param_indices[i]] = theta[i]; return circuit_builder.evaluate_energy(None, p)
Pass x0 = [self.current_params[idx] for idx in active_param_indices] as the initial point to minimize()
After optimization, write result.x back ONLY into self.current_params[active_param_indices], leaving all other positions unchanged (= 0)
Build the final circuit with the updated self.current_params before calling simulator.compute_energy()
Unit test: with a 1-operator circuit and run_classical_opt=True, the optimizer must only vary 1 parameter; other params in self.current_params must remain 0 after the step

objectives.description: Remove or bypass the circuit.ucc shortcut in TencirchemCISimulator.compute_energy()

The preferred implementation: compute_energy() should call circuit.ucc.energy(circuit.params) ONLY if circuit.params is guaranteed to have zeros for non-active operators — ensure this invariant is documented and tested

howTencirchemWorksForPartialCircuits.explanation: tencirchem.UCCSD.energy(params) evaluates exp(T(params) - T†(params))|HF⟩ where T(params) = sum_i params[i] * T_i. If params[j] = 0 for operator j, then operator j contributes nothing to the circuit. Therefore, calling ucc.energy(partial_params) where partial_params[j]=0 for all non-selected operators IS the correct and efficient way to evaluate the energy of the partial circuit. No new UCCSD object needs to be created.
howTencirchemWorksForPartialCircuits.implication: Both evaluate_energy(circuit, params) = ucc.energy(params) and compute_energy shortcut are physically correct IF AND ONLY IF params has zeros for non-selected operators at the time of the call. The entire fix therefore reduces to: ensure the optimizer never writes non-zero values into the inactive parameter slots.

fixSummary.step1: In environment.step(), extract active_param_indices from self.active_parameters (or from self.excitation_to_param_idx for self.current_excitations). Only optimize these indices.
fixSummary.step2: The energy function passed to minimize() should: copy self.current_params, overwrite only active slots with theta, call circuit_builder.evaluate_energy(None, p).
fixSummary.step3: After minimize(), copy result.x back into self.current_params[active_param_indices] only.
fixSummary.step4: In compute_energy(), either (a) remove the hasattr(circuit,'ucc') shortcut entirely, or (b) keep it but add an assertion that circuit.params has zeros at non-active indices — document this invariant clearly.
fixSummary.step5: No changes needed to evaluate_energy itself — ucc.energy(partial_params) is correct.

physicalExpectation.note: For LiH active_space=(2,5) STO-3G, UCCSD = FCI because there are only 2 correlated electrons. The dominant correlation is a doubles excitation (HOMO→LUMO pair). With the corrected environment, the RL agent should discover that 1 correctly-chosen doubles excitation (with its parameter optimized) may actually achieve chemical accuracy for this specific small molecule. However, a randomly chosen single excitation (orbital-diagonal) will NOT reach chemical accuracy. The test of the fix is: does the ENERGY DEPEND ON WHICH OPERATOR IS SELECTED? After the fix, it must.
